text:
Overview

You must provide workers in Great Britain with a statement informing them of their right to join a trade union. This is to comply with section 136A Trade Union and Labour Relations (Consolidation) Act 1992 and the Statement of Trade Union Rights Regulations 2026.

From 1 January 2027, you must give the statement to new workers alongside the written statement of employment particulars.

By 5 April 2027, you must give the statement to existing workers (those employed immediately before 1 January 2027).

From 6 April 2027, as well as giving the statement to all new workers at the same time as the written statement of employment particulars, you must also give the statement to your other workers, or remind them of its availability and location, by 5 April each year. There are different ways employers can meet this annual requirement which are explained in the following guidance.

Preparing a statement to inform workers of their right to join a trade union

You must use the standardised statement to inform workers of their right to join a trade union. You must not add further information to, or change the statement, except where the regulations require or permit this, as outlined in the following sections.

Recognised trade unions

If you recognise trade unions

Where the employer recognises one or more trade unions, the recognised trade unions section of the statement must include:

the name of each trade union recognised by the employer for the purpose of collective bargaining – employers must include all trade unions recognised across their organisation, even where a particular recognition agreement does not cover the worker receiving the statement

a summary of the worker categories and workplace locations covered by each recognition arrangement. The summary should help workers to identify the worker groups and workplace locations covered

at least 2 contact details for each recognised trade union, where these have been provided by the union. These may include a general telephone number, a general email address, or a physical office location (such as a physical room at an employer) or address of the trade union

You are encouraged to discuss with the relevant recognised trade unions how best to reflect the recognition arrangements in the statement.

Preparing the recognised trade union contact details

You should request the relevant contact details from the union. Where the union does not provide them, the employer should omit those contact details from the statement.

Recognised trade unions are encouraged to provide these contact details within a reasonable time following a request from the employer. Where a new recognition arrangement is reached, recognised trade unions are encouraged to provide the contact details within 14 days of the recognition being arranged.

The trade union must ensure that the contact details do not include personal contact information, such as the name of an individual.

You may agree with a recognised trade union to provide different general contact details of that union to different groups of workers, where appropriate. For example, workers in different regions could be given contact details for their relevant regional union office. This approach is optional.

Where recognition is being sought but has not yet been agreed or determined, the name and details of the union seeking recognition should not be included in the statement until recognition is in place.

If you do not recognise a trade union

If you do not recognise any trade union, you must state that the employer does not recognise any trade unions for the purposes of collective bargaining.

Statutory access agreements

Statutory access agreements (those made under Chapter 5ZA of Part 1 of the 1992 Act) provide for trade union officials to enter a workplace, communicate with workers, or both, for specified purposes.

If you have a statutory access agreement with a trade union

The statutory access agreements section of the statement must include:

the name of each trade union that has a statutory access agreement with the employer. Employers must include all unions with statutory access agreements, even where a particular access agreement does not cover the worker receiving the statement

at least 2 contact details for each union that has a statutory access agreement with the employer, where these have been provided by the union. These may include a general telephone number, a general email address, or a physical office location (such as a physical room at an employer) or address of the trade union

Preparing the trade union contact details

You should request the relevant contact details from the union. Where the union does not provide them, the employer should omit those contact details from the statement.

Trade unions with access agreements are encouraged to provide these contact details within a reasonable time frame following a request from the employer. Where a new statutory access agreement is reached, trade unions are encouraged to provide the contact details within 14 days of the access agreement being agreed.

The trade union must ensure that their contact details do not include personal contact information, such as the name of an individual.

You may agree with a trade union to provide different general contact details of that union to different groups of workers, where appropriate. For example, workers in different regions could be given contact details for their relevant regional union office. This approach is optional.

Where a statutory access agreement is being sought but has not yet been agreed or determined, the name and details of the union seeking that agreement should not be included in the statement until the agreement is in place.

As a matter of good practice, you are encouraged to provide workers with information about trade unions with which you have non-statutory access arrangements separately from the statement.

If you do not have a statutory access with a trade union

If you do not have a statutory access agreement with any trade union, you must state that there are no statutory access agreements.

Finding a trade union

You must provide either:

details of the webpage on which the Certification Officer’s official list of trade unions is published

a copy of the Certification Officer’s list alongside the statement

The official list of trade unions is made under a statutory obligation by the Certification Officer, the independent statutory regulator of trade unions.

Providing the webpage to the Certification Officer’s list

If you choose to provide details of the Certification Officer’s webpage and the statement is provided electronically, you must include the full web address (https://www.gov.uk/certification-officer-list-of-trade-unions) and a hyperlink to Certification Officer list of trade unions in the ‘Finding a trade union’ section of the statement.

If you choose to provide details of the Certification Officer’s webpage and the statement is provided by non-electronic means, you must include the full web address (https://www.gov.uk/certification-officer-list-of-trade-unions) in the ‘Finding a trade union’ section of the statement.

Providing a copy of the Certification Officer’s list

If you choose to provide a copy of the Certification Officer’s official list of trade unions, you must provide this alongside the statement. You can do this whether the statement itself is provided electronically or by non-electronic means.

You can obtain a copy of the Certification Officer’s list in any of the following ways:

download the official list of trade unions

email the Certification Officer to obtain the list at info@certoffice.org

You can also write to the Certification Officer to obtain the list at:

Certification Office

11th Floor

14 Westfield Avenue

London

E20 1HZ

If you request the list in writing, allow enough time for your request to be received and for the list to be sent to you, while also recognising that the list must be obtained not more than one month before being provided to the worker (see below). The Certification Officer will aim to respond to any requests for the list as soon as reasonably possible and in any event within 14 days of receiving a request. Downloading the list or requesting it by email is quicker than writing to the Certification Officer by post and is recommended where possible.

If you choose to provide a copy of the Certification Officer’s list alongside the statement, the copy must have been obtained from the Certification Officer’s web page or directly from the Certification Officer not more than one month before it is provided to the worker (a month means a calendar month). Although the Certification Officer will update the list occasionally, an updated version only needs to be provided to workers if you subsequently provide the statement directly to workers again. You do not have to provide an update of the list when reminding workers of the availability of the statement and where it is available.

Giving the statement to workers

How and when you give the statement to workers differs depending on whether the worker is starting employment and whether the statement is being provided for the first time or again on a later occasion.

Giving the statement to new workers (beginning employment at any time)

From 1 January 2027 and for all new workers thereafter, you must provide the statement directly to new workers when they start employment at the same time as providing the written statement of employment particulars. The statement is separate from the written statement of employment particulars. This includes new workers starting or re-starting employment with the employer.

You must give the statement to the new worker directly by either:

electronic means

post

in-person delivery

When you have provided the statement to a new worker, you do not need to provide it again during the same annual cycle (6 April to 5 April), unless there are changes to the recognition or access agreement details.

Giving the statement to existing workers by 5 April 2027

Between 1 January and 5 April 2027, you must give the statement to all workers who were already employed by you when the duty came into force on 1 January 2027 and who remain employed on 5 April 2027. You can provide the statement at any point during this period. You can do so by either giving the statement directly or by making the statement continuously available. You do not need to use the same method for all workers and may decide on what you consider to be the most appropriate method for each worker or group of workers.

If you deliver the statement by direct methods, you must use either:

electronic means

post

delivery in person

Examples of making the statement continuously available by making it available on:

an intranet

a shared drive

an internal website

a physical noticeboard

within a physical or online handbook

If you make the statement continuously available, you must make sure that:

by 5 April 2027, the worker is notified in writing that the statement is available and of the location where it can be accessed

the notification includes sufficient information to enable the worker to find the location

the notification is delivered in person, sent by post, or sent by electronic means

the notification is headed “Availability and location of statement of trade union rights” and must be factual and not used to qualify or undermine the statement. You may wish to use the following wording: “A statement informing you of your right to join a trade union is available at the following location: [insert location, including sufficient information to enable the worker to find the location].”

from the time the worker is notified, the statement remains continuously available and reasonably accessible until (and including) 5 April 2027, and can be accessed without the worker having to make a specific request for it

Giving the statement to all workers from 6 April 2027

From 6 April 2027, in addition to providing the statement directly to new workers, you must in each year (6 April to 5 April) and for all workers (other than those who have already been given the statement as a new worker in the relevant year) either:

provide the statement by 5 April each year if a direct delivery method is being used. You only need to provide the statement once during each annual cycle (6 April to 5 April), unless there are changes to the recognition or access agreement details included in the statement

or

make the statement continuously available and reasonably accessible for the whole of the relevant year (6 April to 5 April), for example by making the statement available on an intranet, shared drive, internal website, physical noticeboard or within a physical or online handbook

When making the statement continuously available:

you must notify the worker in writing, on or before 5 April in the annual cycle, that the statement is available and of the location where it can be accessed. You must do this in every annual cycle in which you make the statement continuously available

the notification must include sufficient information to enable the worker to find the location

the notification can be delivered in person, sent by post, or sent by electronic means

the notification must be headed “Availability and location of statement of trade union rights” and must be factual and not used to qualify or undermine the statement. You may wish to use the following wording: “A statement informing you of your right to join a trade union is available at the following location: [insert location, including sufficient information to enable the worker to find the location].”

the statement must remain continuously available and reasonably accessible for the whole of the annual cycle (6 April to 5 April), and must be accessible without the worker having to make a specific request for it

You must also have notified the worker of the availability and location of the statement before the start of the annual cycle (6 April). This is so that workers know where to find the statement before the cycle begins. You do not need to send a separate notification before the start of the annual cycle if the worker received a notification of the availability and location of the statement during the previous annual cycle (6 April to 5 April). This could be either the notification given to existing workers by 5 April 2027, or the notification described above.

This means that, if you make the statement continuously available year after year, one notification in each annual cycle will normally be enough. It counts as the notification for that annual cycle and as the advance notification for the next.

You will need to send a notification before the start of the annual cycle where the worker did not receive one during the previous annual cycle. This will normally be where:

you gave the statement directly to a new worker and wish to make it continuously available for the following annual cycle

you gave the statement directly to the worker in the previous annual cycle and wish to switch to making it continuously available for the new annual cycle

Where a notification is needed before the start of the annual cycle, you must comply with the same requirements as referred to above about the notification including sufficient information to find the location, the means of delivery, the heading of the notification and the factual nature of the notification.

You can choose each year whether to give the statement directly to a worker or make it continuously available. You do not need to use the same method during each annual cycle (6 April to 5 April).

Whether you give the statement directly to a worker or make it continuously available, providing the statement or notification as a standalone communication can help workers more easily identify and access the information. It may also be sent as part of a wider communication.

When to give the statement: summary table

The table provides an overview of the key timing requirements. Read it alongside the full guidance to understand what you need to do.

When Who What to do

From 1 January 2027 New workers Give the statement directly when they start.

Between 1 January and 5 April 2027 Existing workers (those already in employment on 1 January 2027) Give the statement directly or make it continuously available and tell workers in writing where to find it.

From 6 April 2027 New workers Give the statement directly when they start.

From 6 April 2027 Existing workers (those already in employment on 6 April of the relevant year) By 5 April each year, give the statement directly, or if making the statement continuously available, tell workers in writing where to find it.

If the location or detail of the statement changes

Changes to the recognition or access agreements details

Where there is a change to the information required to be included in the statement about recognised trade unions or statutory access agreements, you must update the statement for workers who have previously been given the statement and remain employed by you. You must give workers the entire updated statement, rather than a separate statement or information covering only the changes. The updated statement must be given to these workers within one month beginning with the date on which the change takes effect. A month means a calendar month.

Unless the statement is being made continuously available when the change takes effect, you must update and reissue the statement directly to workers within one month of the change, either in person, by post or by electronic means.

If, when the change takes effect, the statement is being made continuously available and reasonably accessible, you must, within one month of the change, update the statement at the location where it is already being made available.

Where the statement is being made continuously available, workers do not need to be informed separately of the change as long as the location of the statement remains the same as previously communicated.

Once the contact details of a trade union included in the statement change twice in an annual cycle (6 April to 5 April), you do not need to give an updated statement for any further contact detail changes during that annual cycle. This applies separately to each trade union included in the statement.

Changes to the statement location

If the location where the statement is continuously available stops being reasonably accessible due to circumstances beyond your reasonable control, you must:

make the statement available at a new reasonably accessible location

notify workers of the new location as soon as reasonably possible directly and in writing

deliver the notification in person, by post or by electronic means.

include sufficient information in the notification to enable the worker to find the location

make sure the notification is headed “Availability and location of statement of trade union rights” and is factual and not used to qualify or undermine the statement

Examples of circumstances beyond your reasonable control may include:

fire

flood

a cyber incident

unexpected loss of access to an IT system or document repository

the sudden closure of premises

This is not an exhaustive list.

In other circumstances, where the location of the statement changes, you must take the following action:

notify workers directly and in writing of the new location and the date on which the change takes effect within one month in advance of the change of location. A month means a calendar month

include sufficient information in the notification to enable the worker to find the location

deliver the notification in person, by post, or by electronic means

make sure the notification is headed “Availability and location of statement of trade union rights”, is factual and is not used to qualify or undermine the statement. You may wish to use the following wording: “The location of the statement informing you of your right to join a trade union is changing. From [insert date], the statement will be available at the following location: [insert location, including sufficient information to enable the worker to find the location].”

Problems with a statement

If a worker has a problem receiving or being notified about the availability of their statement, or with the content of a statement, they can:

try to solve the problem with their employer informally

if this does not work, take out a grievance against their employer (employers can also get advice about handling grievances)

in circumstances where certain other proceedings are being brought against an employer, take a case to an employment tribunal

Compensation

If a worker wins a case in the other proceedings (for example, unauthorised deductions from their wages), the tribunal may award compensation if the employer has also breached its legal duties relating to the provision of the statement.

Compensation can be up to 4 weeks’ pay although there is a limit on how much a tribunal will award for a week’s pay.

Additional information for workers

As a matter of good practice, you are encouraged to share additional information and resources separately from the statutory statement to help workers understand their right to join a trade union and how they can access further information.

Where there is additional information about a recognised union or union with an access agreement that may be helpful to workers but does not form part of the statement, this can be provided separately. This could include, for example, general contact details for relevant regional or local union offices, or information about non-statutory access arrangements.

Helpful resources include:

Trades Union Congress (TUC) Interactive union finder tool – this can help workers identify trade unions that are relevant to their job, workplace or sector

individual websites of recognised trade unions or trade unions with an access agreement, which provide further information about trade union membership and how workers can join a union

GOV.UK guidance on joining a trade union, which provides information on joining a trade union and trade union membership rights
